chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 49 — The Spirits Resting upon the Chosen One
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text preserved in Rylands Ethiopic MS 23 is the translation base for all four verses, including wisdom poured out like water, the passing of unrighteousness, and the spirits of wisdom, understanding, instruction, might and those who sleep in righteousness resting upon the Chosen One. The compact list of spirits is retained without merging its clauses or supplying an identity beyond the witness. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: For wisdom is poured out like water, and glory does not cease before him forever and ever.
verses.study: Wisdom flows in abundance around the Chosen One, continuing the fountain imagery of Chapter 48. Unending glory accompanies freely poured wisdom rather than secretive scarcity.
crossReferences: Isaiah 11:9 — knowledge of the LORD fills the earth like waters
Joel 2:28 — God promises to pour out His Spirit
John 1:14 — the chosen revealer is full of grace and glory

verses.text: For he is mighty in all the secrets of righteousness, and unrighteousness will pass away like a shadow and have no place to stand, because the Chosen One stands before the Lord of Spirits. His glory is forever and ever, and his power from generation to generation.
verses.study: The Chosen One's enduring stand before the Lord displaces unrighteousness, which proves as insubstantial as a passing shadow. Righteous authority endures because it remains before the divine presence.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:4–5 — the wicked cannot stand in judgment
Isaiah 32:1 — a king reigns in righteousness
Daniel 7:14 — the humanlike ruler receives an enduring dominion

verses.text: In him dwells the spirit of wisdom, the spirit that gives understanding, the spirit of instruction and might, and the spirit of those who sleep in righteousness.
verses.study: Wisdom, understanding, instruction and strength dwell together in the chosen judge. The added spirit associated with the righteous dead joins his rule to the hope of those whose faithful lives have ended.
crossReferences: Isaiah 11:2 — wisdom, understanding, counsel and might rest upon the chosen ruler
Daniel 12:2–3 — those sleeping in the dust rise to differing destinies
Revelation 14:13 — those who die in the Lord rest from their labor

verses.text: He will judge the things that are hidden, and no one will be able to utter an empty word before him, for he is the Chosen One before the Lord of Spirits, according to His good pleasure.
verses.study: Hidden realities and careless speech are both accountable before the Chosen One. His authority is not self-appointed; it rests in the Lord of Spirits' deliberate choice and pleasure.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 12:14 — God brings every hidden thing into judgment
Matthew 12:36 — people give account for every careless word
Isaiah 42:1 — God delights in His chosen servant

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 49 gathers the qualities needed for the Chosen One's judgment. Wisdom is abundant, righteousness is secret yet fully known, and glory and power endure through every generation.
Unrighteousness has no stable existence before him. It passes like a shadow because the Chosen One himself stands continually before the Lord of Spirits.

The resting spirits echo the portrait of the chosen ruler in Isaiah: wisdom, understanding, instruction and might are integrated rather than divided. The reference to those sleeping in righteousness also ties his ministry to the faithful dead.
Judgment reaches concealed deeds and apparently insignificant words. Yet its authority remains relational—the Chosen One judges because he is chosen according to the Lord's good pleasure.

crossReferences: Isaiah 11:2 — the Spirit's gifts upon the chosen ruler
Ecclesiastes 12:14; Matthew 12:36 — hidden deeds and empty words judged
Isaiah 42:1 — the chosen servant who pleases God
